hero.title: Box Breathing: The Ultimate Savior for Severe Pre-sleep Anxiety
hero.description: Is your body exhausted but your brain feels like a spinning carousel? Traditional relaxation often fails under extreme stress. Try Box Breathing—the exact rhythmic breathing used by Navy SEALs in high-stress combat situations. By forcing a 4-4-4-4 isometric rhythm, you wrest back control of your autonomic nervous system and shut down racing thoughts.

mechanism.title: How it works: Hijacking your attention
mechanism.description: During insomnia triggered by anxiety, your brain is in a 'fight or flight' state. Box breathing's four equal phases (inhale, hold, exhale, hold) require tremendous focus. This 'hijacks' your prefrontal cortex, leaving zero cognitive bandwidth for worrying about tomorrow.

items.title: Reset Vagal Tone

items.title: Balance Gas Exchange
items.description: The symmetric rhythm prevents the hyperventilation and breath shortness that usually accompany anxiety.

steps.label: Sleep Practice
steps.title: Draw a 'Breath Box' tonight
steps.description: Visualize a square. With every 4-second phase, you draw one edge of the square.

items.title: Step 1: Inhale (4s)
items.description: Slowly breathe in through your nose. Visualize drawing the left edge of the square (moving up).

items.title: Step 2: Hold Breath (4s)
items.description: Hold the air in your lungs. Visualize drawing the top edge (moving right).

items.title: Step 3: Exhale (4s)
items.description: Slowly release all air through your mouth or nose. Visualize drawing the right edge (moving down).

items.title: Step 4: Hold Empty (4s)
items.description: Hold your breath with your lungs empty. Visualize drawing the bottom edge (moving left) back to the start.

faq.title: FAQs about Box Breathing

items.question: Box Breathing vs 4-7-8 Method: Which should I choose?
items.answer: The difference is the ratio. 4-7-8 emphasizes an 8s exhale specifically to drop your heart rate fast (best for pure physical sleep onset). Box breathing (4-4-4-4) drops heart rate, but excels at 'clearing severe anxiety and rumination' because the equal holds force extreme mental focus. Try both to see which fits your night.

items.question: Is it normal to feel discomfort during the empty-lung hold (step 4)?
items.answer: Yes, totally normal. The retention after exhaling is the strongest trigger for the vagus nerve but also the easiest to cause an instinctual panic. Don't force 4 seconds. You can start with a 3-second box in the app settings and build up.

items.question: Can I use this during a daytime panic attack?
items.answer: Absolutely. Box breathing is a primary acute-intervention strategy recommended by therapists for panic attacks. The solid, predictable rhythm gives a spiraling brain a 'physical anchor'.
